Date of Notice: 2026-08-15
Requested Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Treating Surgeon: [Okafor, MD — practice name and NPI not contained in the records provided]

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472), stated in the above-referenced notice to be based on "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed, because the clinical record does document a lengthy and multi-modal trial of conservative treatment, together with the objective findings that support surgery at this time.

A note on the criteria being addressed: I have not been given, and have not been able to independently confirm, a plan-specific "medical policy" document that 'Ohana Health Plan applied to this request. The most specific publicly available shoulder-arthroplasty medical-necessity criteria I was able to identify are those issued by Evolent (the vendor that performs musculoskeletal prior-authorization review for Wellcare/'Ohana-affiliated plans), titled "Shoulder Arthroplasty," Guideline Number Evolent_CG_1769. Where I quote language below, it is quoted directly from that document. I am not able to confirm from the records whether this is the exact version 'Ohana applied to my case, and I ask 'Ohana to identify, in its response, the specific policy name, number, and version it actually used, and to provide a copy, if this differs from what is addressed below.

1. Duration and severity of symptoms
The guideline's clinical-documentation expectations state that "Clinical notes should address: Symptom onset, duration, and severity[,] Loss of function and/or limitations[,] Type and duration of non-operative management modalities." My record documents 14 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest, with the functional and exam findings described below.

2. Conservative (non-operative) treatment trial
The guideline states that Total Shoulder Arthroplasty may be necessary when there has been "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following: ○ Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program ○ Rest or activity modification ○ Application of heat or ice ○ Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics) ○ Corticosteroid injections."

My record documents all of the following, well in excess of the stated 12-week minimum:
- Supervised physical therapy, 16 weeks (2026-03-08 to 2026-06-28), 24 visits completed, focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-12, which produced only 4 weeks of partial relief.

This is documentation of more than one of the listed modalities, sustained well beyond 12 weeks, with inadequate or only temporary benefit. I ask that the reviewer re-examine the submitted records against this specific criterion, as the denial's statement that conservative treatment was not "adequately" trialed does not appear to be supported by the chart.

3. Imaging findings
The guideline provides that TSA may be necessary with "Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)* ... *NOTE: In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required." Radiographs dated 2026-07-14 (true AP and axillary views) show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid — i.e., bone-on-bone articulation. Under the guideline's own express note, this finding means "non-operative treatment is not required" as a precondition to surgery, which independently supports approval even apart from the extensive conservative trial already completed and documented above.

4. Intact rotator cuff and deltoid function
The guideline requires a "Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan." CT imaging confirms an intact rotator cuff, and examination documents intact cuff strength, satisfying this element.

5. Functional limitation
The guideline's general requirement is that the "Individual has limited function (age-appropriate activities of active daily livings (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)." My record documents that I cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side, and examination shows active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, external rotation limited to 10 degrees, and glenohumeral crepitus.

6. Absence of contraindications
The guideline's general requirements also specify that the individual "does not have an active local or systemic infection," "does not have active, untreated drug dependency," and "is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI." My record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, none of which are noted in the guideline as disqualifying.

Conclusion
Taken together, the submitted records document: (a) 14 months of progressive, functionally limiting shoulder pain; (b) a 16-week, 24-visit supervised physical therapy course; (c) 6 months of NSAID therapy; (d) a corticosteroid injection with only transient benefit; (e) radiographic bone-on-bone glenohumeral disease; (f) an intact rotator cuff on CT and exam; and (g) no medical contraindications to surgery. This directly addresses the stated denial reason regarding an "adequate trial of conservative treatment," and it satisfies each of the elements quoted above from the Evolent Shoulder Arthroplasty guideline (Evolent_CG_1769) to the extent that guideline is what was applied to this request. I ask that 'Ohana Health Plan reverse the denial and approve the requested total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472).

If 'Ohana Health Plan relied on a different medical policy or criteria set than the one addressed above, I ask that this be identified specifically in your response, together with a copy of that document, so that the record can be supplemented as needed within the appeal period.

Enclosed / attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-08 to 2026-06-28)
- Medication and injection records, including the 2026-05-12 corticosteroid injection note
- Radiology report, shoulder radiographs, 2026-07-14
- CT report confirming intact rotator cuff
- Office examination notes documenting range of motion, crepitus, and functional limitation
- [Any letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor — not contained in the records provided]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing. Consistent with the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination, I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-11, and I am submitting it well within that deadline. Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address/phone number below.

If my condition requires a more urgent (expedited) review, please advise me immediately of the process for requesting one, as the notice provided to me did not describe expedited-appeal procedures.

Sincerely,

Taylor Jennings
